fran: Strange repro today: not only do blocked auth refreshes cause handshake stalls, but we can hit a goroutine leak even after ctx cancel if the generator is blocked writing to the stream channel (backpressure + cancel interplay). Repro below.

fran: ```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
creds := &slowCreds{delay: 2 * time.Second} // blocks without ctx support
cli := NewClient(WithCreds(creds))
g, _ := cli.Generator(ctx, "small")
stream, _ := g.Stream(ctx)
// consumer intentionally doesn't drain to simulate blocked receiver
go func() { time.Sleep(100 * time.Millisecond); cancel() }()
// generator internals: sends into stream.ch which is unbuffered -> send blocks if receiver not draining
// observed: handshake goroutine + send goroutine stuck even after cancel.
```

devon: Interesting. So there are two separate failure modes that can cascade: (1) creds blocking handshake, (2) generator send into stream.Chan blocks if consumer stopped reading. If both happen, cancellation can leave in-flight goroutines stuck.

kevin: Yep. Our current Stream impl does something like `for tok := range src { streamCh <- tok }` with an unbuffered channel and no select on ctx for the internal send path. If the consumer cancels and stops draining, that internal send blocks forever.

rachel: UX-wise we should avoid leaving users with subtle leaks. Ideas: (A) make internal sends context-aware (select on ctx or abort channel); (B) use a modestly buffered stream channel (e.g., 16) to tolerate temporary stalls; (C) provide an explicit Stream.Close()/Abort() that drains/cleans up; (D) document the "drain or Close" pattern in onboarding sample apps.

fran: I prototyped a fix: change internal send to `select { case streamCh <- tok: case <-ctx.Done(): return }` and add buffer=8. That solves the deadlock in repro. But we must be careful about API semantics: when we drop tokens due to cancel we should return a clear error to the user (ErrStreamAborted) so apps don't silently lose output.

devon: Also consider the case where user calls cancel but then inspects the returned stream later: should Stream() return an error immediately on cancel or return a closable stream that yields no messages? We need clear contract. Current behavior is inconsistent across SDKs.

kevin: For parity and DX I'd propose: 1) Stream(ctx) should return quickly with ErrCanceled if ctx already canceled. 2) After Stream() starts, generator should ensure it can be aborted by either ctx.Done() or Generator.Abort(); aborted streams should close the channel and set an error state (ErrStreamAborted) observable via the stream API. 3) Internally use small buffer + context-aware sends so a transient consumer pause doesn't leak.

rachel: Also we should update onboarding sample app to show "drain-on-cancel" pattern and the correct Close/Abort usage. Example snippet for README: `defer func(){ g.Abort(); for range stream.Chan(){ } }()` — ensure client code never leaves a goroutine blocked on send.

fran: I'll open a PR that: a) makes internal stream sends select on ctx, b) sets a default buffer size to 8, c) adds Generator.Abort() which closes an internal abort channel, d) returns explicit ErrAuthCanceled / ErrStreamAborted error types, and e) adds a unit test that simulates slow creds + blocked consumer and asserts no goroutine leaks.

sam: Please also add a small sample app in sdk/examples/onboarding that demonstrates both patterns: using `context.WithTimeout` for handshake and `defer g.Abort()` + draining the channel. That will help users avoid the trap.

kevin: CI note: canary e2e showed goroutine growth in generator tests when we ran user-simulated blocked consumers. I filed INF-7123 and added the repro artifact. ci-bot: plz link to INF-7123.

ci-bot: [ci-bot] Canary detected generator goroutine regression on canary-e2e. Created INF-7123: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-7123

devon: Minor API ergonomics question: should Abort() be named Close() or Interrupt()? I prefer Abort() to signal abrupt termination; Close() often implies graceful finish. Thoughts?

rachel: Agree with Abort() naming. Also ensure Abort() is idempotent and safe to call after Stream returns (no-op). Document it clearly.

fran: One more DX item: add an error help hint when we return ErrStreamAborted: "Possible causes: blocking credentials, consumer not draining stream, or explicit Abort(). See onboarding docs: /sdk/go/cancellation-and-streaming". That should reduce support noise.

kevin: Good. Let's land the small change (context-aware send + buffer + Abort shim) as a non-breaking improvement, then follow up with creds.GetToken(ctx) migration in the next sprint. Put the leak-detection unit test and sample-app update in the same PR to keep the regression from reappearing.

fran: Thanks all. I'll assign the PR to @devon and tag the SDK parity board. Leaving repro and logs in the INF ticket.

sam: :thumbsup: great plan.
